newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria tenders for import of 50,000T wheat.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria tenders for import of 50,000T wheat.

text.p: Bulgaria has called a tender to import 50,000 tonnes of wheat in exchange for exports from the new harvest, state news agency BTA said on Friday.

BTA quoted Agriculture Minister Roumen Hristov as saying the interim cabinet would not import U.S. bread wheat under the U.S. Department of Agriculture's GSM-102 export credit guarantee programme as the price of more than $210 per tonne was too high. He said negotiations would be held with Hungary, as the price would be $190.
Earlier this week, officials said the country now needed about 100,000 tonnes of wheat to cover the gap until the new crop.
Another tender for importing 50,000 tonnes of wheat is expected to be called by the end of this month but the terms are yet to be decided upon, officials said.
Both deals are to be guaranteed by the government through the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development through a stable state-owned bank, probably the country's biggest Bulbank.
